newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- U.S. T-bond vols ease,Nov expires quietly.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- U.S. T-bond vols ease,Nov expires quietly.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. T-bond futures options were slighly lower in late-morning trade Friday as traders began to discount prices for time decay ahead of the weekend.
At 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, implied volatility for December T-bond options was down less that a tenth of a percentage point on the day at 9.57 percent but expected to drift lower.
The expiration of November serial options was proceeding quietly and may have been helping to subdue futures prices, according to dealers at Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
Brad Tyl, senior vice president at Aubrey G Lanston, said open interest in November 111-00 calls -- which are in-the-money -- was 22,000 going into today's session.
"I think that's probably what's holding us back from advancing as we speak. They're taking a little bit of their profits as the day is wearing on," he said.
Open interest in November 111-00 puts was 6,500, he said.

Among the day's largest trades was a large calendar spread done 2000 times by a large investment house. The house bought March 106-00 puts and sold December 110-00 puts. Another house did the same trade 8000 times on Thursday, dealers said.
One dealer believes the market will be driven by news out of Europe and continued speculation about the Fed's intentions next week, as the U.S. economic calendar is light.
"We don't really see any opportunities for economic indicators to be moving the market in any direction," he said. "Extraneous information is going to be what's driving the markets."
Implied volatilities for eurodollar options were holding steady at Chicago Mercantile Exchange, which surprised some dealers.

"I thought they would take it (time decay) out over this weekend and I'm really not seeing it," one CME dealer said. "I still think they're going to settle this stuff at least unchanged and they might even try to take it down an eighth."
He quoted December Eurodollar volatility -- based on the 94.25 strike -- at 10.75 percent and March at 14.65 percent.
